args.notes: Tight accuracy spec: max_abs_err <= 2^-20 (~9.54e-7) at >=50 MSPS. Precision comes from data width and iteration count, not from unrolling; area is the primary objective (min luts_plus_ffs) with power_index secondary. Prefer small-width iterative/pipelined families with enough fractional bits; avoid large unroll factors that inflate LUTs. Ensure the front is well spread and feasible on both constraints.

args.lesson: Spec high_precision (max_abs_err <= 2^-20, >=50 MSPS, min luts_plus_ffs then min power_index): run_dse with the full 400 evals (4 rounds, map_front x3 then stop) returned a single feasible non-dominated design, pipelined_m:data_width=27,n_iter=22,angle_guard=0,frac_guard=0,rounding=trunc,m=7 -> luts_plus_ffs=2340, power_index=4.4, throughput_msps=52, max_abs_err=7.54e-07 (2^-20.34). L3/L4/L5 had no recorded rows for this design (W=27 exhaustive verify too heavy live; L4 never run live), so back_annotate returned no_measured_data and flagged no winner change -> no reexplore. Lesson: for very tight-accuracy specs the structured graph converges to one design quickly; the front is thin, so extra explore_family calls would likely be wasted, and the ladder is a no-op when no measured rows exist.
